2. Facts, in short, are that respondent Nos. 1 and 2 as plaintiffs brought Title Suit No. 211 of 1981 for declaration that the alleged deed of gift is illegal, void and has been made upon false personation only to deprive the plaintiffs of their lawful properties and, as such, the defendant Nos. 1-4 be directed to evict from the suit property. Plaintiff's case is that property measuring 0.26 acres of land comprised in Plot Nos. 240 and 160 under CS Khatian No. 166 and Hal Mutation Khatian No. 77/4 within Mouza-Morail within Police Station and District-Brahmanbaria with one old building and also 0.51 acres of land comprised in Plot No. 151 within same Khatian, being a pond, total measuring 0.31 acres of land were originally owned and possessed by one Srimati Bimala Banik and her five sons who took Taka 925 as loan from one Kailash Chandra Banik and secured the said loan by mortgaging her property including the suit property and also executed a registered Tamsuk in favour of said Kailash Chandra Banik. Plaintiffs further stated in the plaint that Kailash Chandra Banik was the Korta of the Hindu joint family of the 3 brothers namely, Kailash Chandra Banik, Nabin Chandra Banik and Gobinda Chandra Banik all sons of Ram Kumar Banik. Kailash Chandra Banik being the Korta of the joint Hindu family made the loan to said Bimala Banik and others from the fund of joint property. Thereafter, Kailash Chandra died leaving behind his only son Nabaddip Chandra Banik and his brothers. In the meantime, the aforesaid loanee Bimala Banik failed to pay the loan along with interest for which Nabin Chandra Banik instituted Title Suit No. 506 of 1917 in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Comilla, which was ultimately decreed on 25-11-1918 AD in favour of the plaintiff Nabaddip Chandra Banik. Plaintiffs' further case is that Sree Nabaddip Chandra Banik purchased the entire mortgaged property and the sale certificate was issued in his favour on 20-7-1920 and the sale was duly confirmed by the executing Court. Thereafter, the plaintiff/auction purchaser Nabaddip Chandra Banik was put to possession of the entire auction sold property including the suit property and the same was being possessed as joint Hindu family property. In the meantime, Nabin Chandra Banik died leaving behind wife Muktamayee, who died later, left two in the family namely the other brother Gobinda Chandra Banik and the son of Kai lash Chandra Banik (aforesaid Nabaddip Chandra Banik). At this stage, the plaintiff asserts that there was amicable settlement of the entire joint property of the said family in between the Survivor Gobinda Chandra Banik and heirs of Kailash Chandra Banik namely Nabaddip Chandra Banik in the year 1959 upon which Gobinda Chandra Banik got the Saham of the suit property and the said Nabaddip Chandra Banik got the Saham of landed property situated at Bazarghat in the District of Agartala, India since the said Nabaddip Chandra Banik left the then East Pakistan and migrated to Bazarghat for ever and never returned back to this part of the Country. The plaintiff further asserts that pursuant to the said amicable settlement the said Gobinda Chandra Banik while possessing his Saham property, sold some portion of the property to others and thereafter during the RS operation the name of said Gobinda Banik son of Ram Kumar Banik was correctly recorded in RS Khatian being No. 83 who thereafter paid rent and taxes in his own name. The aforesaid Gobinda Chandra Banik had three sons namely, the plaintiffs Naresh Chandra Banik, Dharesh Chandra Banik and father of the defendant Nos. 1-4 namely Paresh Chandra Banik. Out of them Paresh Chandra Banik was living in the joint family with his four sons namely, Provash Chandra Banik, Suvash Chandra Banik, Chandan Chandra Banik and Khokan Chandra Banik, who are the defendants Nos. 1-4 of the instant suit. Later the said Paresh Chandra died during the life time of his father Gobinda Chandra Banik. In the year 1970 Gobinda Chandra Banik at his old age executed a deed of gift in favour of plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2, who are his living sons, being registered deed of gift No. 4802 dated 5-6-1970, through which he gifted away all his properties to the plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 and handed over possession of the same to them including the residential house, on the ground that the defendant Nos. 1-4 are arrogant and regularly making trouble to the plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2. Thereafter, the plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 mutated their names through Miscellaneous Case No. 493 of 1979-80 and obtained separated mutation khatian No. 77/4 in respect of suit Plot Nos. 160 and 161 in their names along with other properties and paid rent and taxes. Plaintiffs further assert that the defendant Nos. 1-4 being in permissible possession of the suit property under them refused to vacate the property on demand, on the ground that they have obtained registered deed of gift from Nabaddip Chandra Banik on 1-11-1978 and, as such, they are the rightful possessor and title holder of the suit property. Plaintiffs assert that the said deed of gift is a forgery and obtained by false personating only to deprive the plaintiffs of their lawful properties and the defendant Nos. 1-4 are liable to be evicted from the suit property. Hence they instituted the instant suit. 

 3. The defendant No. 1 Sree Provash Chandra Banik contested the suit by filing written statement, contending, interline„ that complicated question of law related to title and possession in respect of the suit property having been involved in the suit, absence of any prayer regarding either declaration of title or establishment of the same, made the suit non maintainable. The defendant No. 1 further asserts that the family of the three brothers Kailash Chandra Banik, Nabaddip Chandra Banik and Gobinda Chandra Banik was not a joint Hindu family and, as such, Kailash was not the Karta of the said family, rather Kailash from his own fund gave loan of Taka 925 to Bimala Banik and to her five sons upon obtaining mortgage of the property, owned by the said loaner, including the suit property for which after the death of said Kailash, when the loanee failed to pay back the loan amount, the aforesaid Nabaddip for his own interest instituted mortgage Title Suit No. 506 of 1917 and obtained the decree in the said suit, put the same in execution by way of auction and purchased the suit property on public auction through the Court and obtained the sale certificate and delivery of possession which was duly conformed by the executing Court. Thereafter, while Nabaddip Chandra Banik owning and possessing the suit property executed a deed of gift in favour of the defendant Nos. 1-4 on 1-11-1978 through which the defendant Nos. 1-4 obtained right, title and possession in 0.26 acres of land with 50% of the residential building and also 0.05 acres of land in the pond. Thereafter, Nabaddip died leaving behind his four sons, the defendant Nos. 5-8 namely, Sankar, Sukumar, Samorendra and Sattyendra Chandra Banik. The defendant No. 1 asserts that although the plaintiff sold some portion of the property under the suit khatian to strangers but none of them got any right, title or possession in the suit property as the plaintiffs had no right, title and possession in the suit property. The plaintiffs being the first paternal uncle of the defendant Nos. 1-4 residing in a portion of the residential house within the suit property under permissive possession of the defendant Nos. 1-4 and the defendant No. 1 has been in exclusive possession in 0.34 acres of land covered by the deed of gift with entire 50% building thereon and 0.05 acres of land in the tank and he is possessing four rooms of the residential building on the western part and the plaintiffs are in a permissive possession under the defendant No. 1 in two rooms in the eastern portion of the building and two houses of two CI sheet. The defendant No. 1 prayed for dismissal of the suit.
